title: One date, five calendars of antiquity
intro: Ancient historians dated an event by the Olympiad, by the years from the founding of Rome, by the reign of a king. Choose a date in the Julian calendar, counted in years before the common era, and see the same day as an Olympiad and its year (the Olympic year starting in midsummer), as a year ab urbe condita (Varro's era, Rome founded in 753 BCE), as a year of the Hebrew world era (anno mundi), as a year of the era of Nabonassar used by Ptolemy (from 747 BCE) and as a Julian Day Number. Try the battle of Salamis, late September 480 BCE, or the first Olympic games, summer 776 BCE.
amLabel: Year of the Hebrew era (anno mundi)
nabLabel: Year of the era of Nabonassar
